description: Space Diaries is a solo storytelling project focused on ''Abandoned but Not Forgotten'' NASA challenges. I will be creating fictional diaries and creative stories of historical spacecraft left on the Moon and Mars, combining scientific data with creative writing.
summary: Space Diaries: Silent Sentinels of the Sky is an interactive digital storybook designed to introduce school aged space enthusiasts to NASA’s historic hardware left behind on the Moon and Mars. To address the challenge, we transformed real NASA mission telemetry, timelines, and scientific discoveries into connected, first-person diary entries told from the perspective of three iconic explorers: the Apollo 11 Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector (LRRR), the Opportunity Rover, and the InSight Lander. Each emotional mission log is paired with an authentic NASA Science Fact Card, archival mission photography, and custom illustrations, showing how each explorer passed the torch of discovery from the Moon to the Red Planet. This project is important because it bridges technical space data with empathetic storytelling, inspiring the next generation of young explorers to connect with humanity’s ongoing journey in space.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:
Space Diaries: Silent Sentinels of the Sky is an interactive digital storybook that brings NASA’s abandoned lunar and Martian hardware to life for school-aged space enthusiasts. Instead of presenting dry technical tables, the book uses a connected "relay race of discovery" narrative across three iconic missions: the Apollo 11 Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector (LRRR), the Opportunity Rover, and the InSight Lander. Each chapter features a first-person mission log written from the spacecraft's perspective—passing the torch of exploration from the Moon to Mars—paired with an authentic NASA Science Card displaying real telemetry, mission timelines, scientific discoveries, and archival photography. The book concludes with an interactive "Young Explorer's Log" prompt encouraging children to design future space missions.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
Young learners often struggle to connect with complex space engineering and raw mission data. By giving silent machines relatable voices and emotions while keeping scientific facts accurate, the project fosters curiosity, STEM engagement, and emotional empathy for humanity's space heritage.

Creativity & Design Factors:
We combined real NASA mission photography with child-friendly character illustrations and readable typography on a space-themed dark blue canvas to create a museum-like yet accessible storybook experience. We carefully ensured scientific accuracy (such as the 532 nm green laser wavelength, 3.8 cm annual lunar drift, 5,111 Sols duration, and 1,319 marsquakes) while maintaining age-appropriate storytelling.

Tools & Software Used:

  • Canva: Used for storybook layout, typography, visual composition, and generating the 27-second presentation video.
  • NASA Open Data & Image Archives: Used for authentic mission photographs, coordinates, and scientific telemetry.
  • Google Gemini: Used for brainstorming the narrative structure, refining English educational copy, and generating custom child-friendly character illustrations (clearly labeled with watermarks inside the project).
